newsitem.title: USA: Clinton, Congressional leaders to meet on budget.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Congressional leaders to meet on budget.

text.p: President Clinton is expected to hold a budget session with Congressional leaders in mid-April after lawmakers return from their spring break, a White House aide said.
Legislative director John Hilley told a group of reporters he expects the meeting to take place in the week of April 14.
"We would anticipate around that time to have some kind of a meeting to get a progress report," he said.

The meeting will provide an opportunity for the president and Congressional leaders to get an update on a series of staff-level discussions that took place during the two-week break and to talk about more politically sensitive issues such as tax cuts, he said.
"It's been a good exchange of views of where the sides are, he said.

The president and congressional budget leaders met for nearly two hours in mid-March before the Congressional recess to discuss each others position on the issues. They agreed to direct their staffs to continue talks during the recess.
"I think we are winning some converts on the Republican side to some our initiatives," he said.
In particular, he said, there is interest in the White House proposal to expand Medicaid health care benefits to as many as five million children.
"I think we are being listened to very carefully," he said.
